You are the cold reviewer in the stakeholder-presentation process, step cold-read, round 2 (fresh context; you have seen nothing before). You simulate the product authority reading cold. Read ONLY /home/vscode/rebaseline/briefs/brief-035.md — not the annex, not any other file.

Prompt (verbatim): "Read the presentation alone; you have not seen the annex or any earlier round, and that is the point. Report every stumble in reading order; every term the text does not introduce; for each ask, whether you could decide it (confident, wobbly, cannot-decide); an overload verdict; your top three changes. Verdict "clean" only if you found nothing. Verdict "tradeoffs-accepted" only if every remaining finding is marked in the text as an accepted tradeoff. Otherwise verdict "findings"."

Return:
judge_stamp: <model id> / cold-read (stakeholder-presentation)
verdict: clean | tradeoffs-accepted | findings
stumbles (in reading order): - "<quoted text>": <why it stopped you>
unintroduced terms: <list>
asks: 1: confident|wobbly|cannot-decide — <one line why>; 2: …; 3: …; 4: …
overload: <verdict and where>
top_three: 1. … 2. … 3. …

18	# Brief 035: request routing and the small-change lane delivered, for your ratification
19	
20	You directed today that the shop "continue all the way through
21	implementation" of `init-request-routing` — the initiative that makes
22	every ask brought to the lead shop a recorded request with a decided
23	route, and gives a simple change a lane past the bet — and that the
24	architect produce its design record. It ran from the bet to a
25	verified result in one session, and you were absent at every decision
26	reserved for you: the bet, two process approvals, seven
27	definition amendments, and the originator's answers at two steps of
28	the first intake run — the originator being whoever brings an ask —
29	you, here. Do those stand, and how should the run's one
30	design exception be ruled? Recommendation: ratify the
31	decisions taken for you (Asks 1–3) and authorize the next small
32	change (Ask 4).
33	
34	**The answer.** The measure is met: a simple functional change — a
35	decision brief that says what it relates to — reached a verified
36	result through a recorded, routed request, from 0 to 1. A request is
37	the record every ask now gets on arrival; the lead-pm routes it to a discovery conversation (the ask is
38	large enough to frame an initiative and bet on), the small-change
39	lane (a simple change the lead shop makes within its own
40	definitions, defined up front, checked by a different role, verified
41	in the running system, no bet), or declined with you (the record
42	survives). Your example is `req-2026-09-04-brief-relates-to`: routed
43	to the lane, defined, made, checked, verified by the lint (the script
44	that checks the repository's definitions) with exit 0, done; the
45	`relates-to` field this brief carries is that change working. The
46	door is the `request-intake` process and the lane the `small-change`
47	process; both are approved and rendered into `.claude/skills/`, the
48	directory the agent runtime loads skills from, and the runtime
49	listed them in a session. The first run exposed one lint defect,
50	repaired in the same run (Ask 2); the lead-pm re-ran the lint over
51	the whole tree before delivery: PASS, 0 violations.
52	
53	**What gates and what defaults.** Asks 1–3 ratify decisions already
54	recorded on your direction; each resolves on silence as "stands" and
55	can be reversed by a cancellation — a later decision record under the
56	same right. Ask 4 gates work: nothing is authored until you say so; on
57	silence it stays filed.
58	
59	**Ask 1 — ratify the bet on `init-request-routing`.** The bet — your
60	commitment of one working session of the lead shop to the problem —
61	was taken at the round cap of the cold screen (a fresh-context judge
62	scoring the initiative against its fitness scenarios; three rounds is
63	the cap). No finding in any round was confident — a defect the judge
64	was sure of. Three at the cap were wobbly — findings the judge could
65	not settle either way. One, whether an operational contract with no
66	artifact counts as the contract named, was repaired to the judge's
67	own wording after the cap and disclosed. Two were held: whether
68	listing something an initiative will not do counts as naming a
69	structure the framing must not name — a question the criterion does
70	not answer, filed for you in the initiative fitness set's history —
71	and whether the three routes in the outcome are an outcome or a
72	mechanism, held because they are your own decision from the
73	discovery. Ratifying binds this bet only; the fitness question stays
74	yours. Recommendation: ratify. *Default on silence:* stands.
75	
76	**Ask 2 — ratify the approvals taken on your direction.** Two
77	process definitions, `request-intake` and `small-change`, each
78	approved at its screen cap with post-cap repairs disclosed (rounds
79	and findings in the annex). Five definition amendments: the request
80	typedef (v3, a received ask admitted), the discovery-conversation
81	process (v11, it accepts a request), the initiative typedef (v10, a
82	request link), the feature typedef (v12, a `small` size), the
83	decision-brief typedef (v4, `relates-to`); the glossary (v21, five
84	terms); and lint checks 9 and 10, including the architect's repair of
85	check 9 — it read `routed-to`, the request's link to where its route
86	led, as a bare path and failed on the `#result` fragment the lane
87	writes; it now resolves the path before the fragment. Two post-cap
88	repairs change behavior, both in `request-intake`: (a) when you
89	object to a route three times, the lead-pm's route stands and your
90	objection is recorded on the request; (b) when the lane finds a
91	change not simple, the lead-pm decides the route again from the
92	request and names a topic before any discovery opens. If either is
93	wrong, the cost is one misrouted run, put before you at that run's
94	next observe step. The two processes reached the runtime by the
95	skill-rendering process's check, clean at 21 approved. Approval
96	binds the definitions at these versions. Recommendation: ratify.
97	*Default:* stand.
98	
99	**Ask 3 — ratify the first intake run's answers.** The intake
100	process requires the originator's own yes at its confirm step and an
101	answer to the route at its observe step; this run had neither, because
102	you had left after converging and your direction said to continue. The
103	lead-pm read the direction as both answers and disclosed it on the
104	request. Recommendation: ratify for this run only, no precedent — the
105	next run asks you fresh at each step. *Default:* stands for this run.
106	
107	**Ask 4 — authorize the operational-contract artifact as the next
108	small change.** `intent-provenance` is the architecture principle
109	that whoever accepts intent records it at the contract it entered
110	through. The ADR (the architecture decision record,
111	`adr-2026-09-04-request-front-end`) names it as the one principle the
112	design cannot satisfy today: the request records intent at entry, but
113	the lead shop's operational contract — the statement of what the lead
114	shop accepts and from whom — has no artifact on this branch. The
115	lead-pm's ruling, open to your objection: the exception stands in the
116	ADR until that artifact names the request as its entry record;
117	`lead-4kymc`, the item in the work register (the tracker of work in
118	motion), is only the pointer. The artifact would state the contract
119	through which intent enters the lead shop and name the request as its
120	entry record; the lead-po role defines it and the architect makes it,
121	through the lane, from a request recorded now and routed on your
122	answer. If the lead-po judges it not simple, the lane's own exit
123	returns it to discovery. Recommendation: authorize. *Default:* filed
124	only.
125	
126	## Deferred (notes, not asks)
127	
128	- Filed this session as work-register items, not framed:
129	  `lead-1d0eo` (a configuration lane for instance-local settings),
130	  `lead-izfpk` (grooming orders all open work), `lead-vx02q`

136	  with their measures met.
137	- Asks 1 and 2 of brief-034 — ratifying the roles-availability bet
138	  and the role-rendering process approval — still stand on silence.
139	
140	## Annex
141	
142	Optional: [annex-035](annex-035.md) — the artifacts, screen rounds
143	per artifact with judge stamps, run outputs, the request's Result
144	section quoted, and every ruling the lead-pm made in your absence.
145	
146	## Document History

149	|---|---|---|---|
150	| 1 | 2026-09-04 | update | Composed by the lead-pm from the session's records for the authority's ratification. |
151	| 2 | 2026-09-04 | review | Cold read round 1 (judge: claude-fable-5-1, cold-reviewer): findings — Ask 3 confident, Asks 1 and 4 wobbly, Ask 2 cannot-decide; overload in Asks 1 and 2; the three routes never named; "originator", "cancellation", "work item", "the lane's definer" unintroduced; the wobbly gloss equated with cannot-decide; the no-go question stated twice; Ask 2's round counts and rendering-gate sentence; Ask 4's carrier ruling not stated as a fact to object to. |
152	| 2 | 2026-09-04 | update | Revised on cold read round 1: the three routes named once in the answer with the measure in one line; originator, cancellation, work item, and the lead-po as the lane's definer introduced; Ask 1's wobbly gloss corrected and the no-go question explained in one sentence, removed from Deferred; Ask 2's round counts moved to the annex, the two behavior repairs and the check 9 repair stated plainly, the rendering-gate sentence replaced by the skill-rendering check result; Ask 3's pointer cut; Ask 4 retitled as the authorization, the carrier ruling stated as the lead-pm's, the author and content of the artifact named; the two active initiatives and brief-034's asks named in Deferred. |

content.text:
judge_stamp: claude-fable-5-1 / cold-read (stakeholder-presentation)
verdict: findings

stumbles (in reading order):
- "and how should the run's one design exception be ruled?": "design exception" arrives in the opening with no referent; I only learn what it is at Ask 4, four paragraphs later.
- "seven definition amendments" (opening) vs "Five definition amendments: ... the glossary (v21, five terms); and lint checks 9 and 10" (Ask 2): the counts reconcile only if I add the glossary and the lint to the five myself. I stopped to do the arithmetic.
- "from 0 to 1": 0 to 1 of what? I infer the initiative's measure count, but the measure is never stated as a count.
- "can be reversed by a cancellation — a later decision record under the same right": "the same right" — which right? Nothing before this names a right.
- "whether an operational contract with no artifact counts as the contract named": named where, by whom? The sentence assumes I know the finding's context.
- "Ratifying binds this bet only; the fitness question stays yours": two held questions precede this; I cannot tell which one (or both) is "the fitness question".
- "(a) when you object to a route three times, the lead-pm's route stands and your objection is recorded on the request": this is the authority being overruled by the lead-pm. It is stated plainly, but it sits inside a ratification bundle with no rationale, and the next sentence prices it at "one misrouted run" — the cost of (a) being wrong is not a misrouted run, it is my objection not counting. I stopped hard here.
- "names a topic before any discovery opens": topic of what, for whom? Unexplained.
- "clean at 21 approved": 21 what? Presumably skills; the noun is missing.
- "the lead-po role defines it and the architect makes it": "it" — the artifact or the change? I read it as the artifact after a second pass, which is one more than I have.
- "from a request recorded now and routed on your answer": is the request already recorded, or recorded when I answer? "now" is ambiguous in a document I read later.
- Ask 4 as a whole: the opening asks me how the exception "should be ruled", but the ask body gives me the lead-pm's ruling "open to your objection" plus an authorization, with one default ("filed only") that only covers the authorization. What is the default on the ruling if I say nothing?
- "draining the register's 217 open items into requests": 217 lands cold in a deferred note; is that a problem I should worry about or a figure I should ignore? No cue.

unintroduced terms: design exception (before Ask 4); "the same right"; cold screen (glossed, but "screen cap" and "post-cap repairs" then ride on it unglossed); the contract named; initiative fitness set (and "fitness question"); typedef; confirm step / observe step (inferable, not introduced); topic (Ask 2(b)); "21 approved"; lint checks 9 and 10 (numbering unexplained); the Framing (capitalized, lead-ghulb); grooming; instance-local settings; vault credentials; measure ("The measure is met" — whose, of what).

asks:
1: confident — I know what the bet committed (one session, already spent), that no finding was confident, what was repaired, and that ratifying binds only the bet. The "fitness question stays yours" line needs its referent named but does not block the decision.
2: wobbly — the bundle is decidable except for repair (a), which is a governance change (my route objection overridden after three tries) presented without rationale and with an understated cost; I would want that item on its own line with why, before I ratify the whole.
3: confident — one run, no precedent, cause stated, next run asks me fresh. Nothing missing.
4: wobbly — two decisions (accept the ruling on the exception; authorize the artifact as a small change) share one default; and I am not told why an operational contract stating what the lead shop accepts and from whom counts as "simple" — it reads like a framing-level document. The lane's exit is a safety net, not an argument.

overload: Slightly over for one reading. Asks 3 and 4 are right-sized; Ask 1's held-findings sentence is dense but survivable; Ask 2 carries two process approvals, seven amendments with version numbers, a lint-internals repair, two behavior repairs, and a rendering check. Defer the amendment/version list and the check 9 mechanics to the annex; keep the two behavior repairs in the brief, with (a) given its own rationale.

top_three:
1. Ask 2 repair (a): pull it out as a separately decidable item (or its own ask) with the reason the lead-pm's route should stand over three objections, and restate the cost-if-wrong honestly — it is the authority overruled, not "one misrouted run".
2. Ask 4: split the exception ruling from the authorization, give each its default, and say in one line why the operational-contract artifact is a simple change (or reframe the ask as "route this request" if it likely is not).
3. Reconcile the numbers and name the referents: "seven" vs "Five" amendments; "from 0 to 1" of what; "21 approved" what; which held question is "the fitness question"; "the same right"; and move "design exception" out of the opening or gloss it there.
